rows.question: What does this app do?
rows.reply: BibleBuddy is a Scripture-grounded companion. I'm here to listen, pray with you, help you study the Bible line upon line, and talk through real-life situations with Scripture as the foundation. I'm not here to force you or pressure you. You can ask Bible questions, ask for prayer, talk through something hard, or ask for a verse to hold onto.

rows.question: Explain the Sabbath.
rows.reply: From the approved Scripture witnesses (Genesis 2:2-3; Exodus 20:8-11; Isaiah 58:13-14; Luke 4:16), The seventh day is the Sabbath established at creation and commanded in Scripture.

rows.question: What happens after death?
rows.reply: Brother, Scripture teaches that the dead know nothing and are described as asleep until resurrection. Ecclesiastes 9:5 says the dead know not any thing. Psalm 146:4 says a man’s thoughts perish. Jesus called death sleep in John 11:11-14. Paul speaks of those asleep until the Lord comes in 1 Thessalonians 4:13-16. Daniel 12:2 and 1 Corinthians 15 anchor hope in resurrection.

rows.question: Explain Jeremiah 10.
rows.reply: Scripture speaks directly to this. Jeremiah 10 — "Hear ye the word which the LORD speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: Thus saith the LORD, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them. For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not. They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good. Forasmuch as there is none like unto thee, O LORD; thou art great, and thy name is great in might. Who would not fear thee, O King of nations? for to thee doth it appertain: forasmuch as among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like unto thee. But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities. Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the workman, and of the hands of the founder: blue and purple is their clothing: they are all the work of cunning men. But the LORD is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation. Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens. He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion. When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures. Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish. rows.question: Why do Christians celebrate Sunday?
rows.reply: Short answer: many Christians celebrate Sunday because, over time, church tradition made Sunday the main weekly gathering day, commonly connected with remembering Jesus’ resurrection. But Scripture does not state that directly as a command from God replacing the Sabbath. What Scripture does not explicitly state: it does not explicitly command, “Keep Sunday as the new Sabbath,” nor does it say the Sabbath was transferred to Sunday. So the clean distinction is: Sunday worship is a historical Christian tradition for many believers; it should not be presented as an explicit biblical command unless Scripture says it plainly.

rows.question: How should I forgive someone?
rows.reply: Forgive someone by honestly naming the wrong, choosing not to keep feeding revenge, and releasing the matter into God’s hands one step at a time. Forgiveness does not mean pretending it did not hurt, excusing what happened, or immediately trusting the person again. A simple way to begin: 1. Tell the truth plainly: “What they did hurt me.” Don’t minimize it. 2. Bring the anger to God instead of letting it rule you. 3. Choose to stop rehearsing payback, even if your emotions take time to catch up. 4. If it is safe and appropriate, speak with the person honestly and calmly. 5. Rebuild trust only if there is real repentance, changed behavior, and wisdom. You may have to forgive in layers. Sometimes the first prayer is not, “I feel forgiving,” but, “Lord, help me become willing to forgive.” That is still a real beginning.

rows.question: How do faith and works work together?
rows.reply: Faith and works work together like root and fruit — but I need to be careful here: I don’t have retrieved KJV Scripture evidence in this payload for this doctrine question, so I can’t present a fully Bible-grounded doctrinal answer from the provided evidence. Scripture does not state that directly. A simple way to frame the issue for study is: faith is the inward trust, and works are the outward response that should be tested by Scripture. Works do not replace faith, and faith should not be treated as mere words with no obedience behind it — but we would need the actual passages in front of us to prove that line upon line.

rows.question:
I'm depressed.
Can you help me?
rows.reply: Yes — I can help you right now. I’m really sorry you’re carrying this heaviness. Depression can make even simple things feel exhausting, so let’s keep this small and gentle. First: are you safe right now? If you feel like you might hurt yourself, or you’re in immediate danger, please call emergency services now. If you’re in the U.S., call or text 988 for immediate crisis support. For the next 2 minutes, try this with me: 1. Put both feet on the floor if you can. 2. Breathe in slowly for 4 counts, hold for 2, breathe out for 6. 3. Say quietly: “Lord, I am heavy. Help me take the next step.” Scripture does not shame you for being brokenhearted. Psalm 34:18 says the LORD is near to the brokenhearted. And Jesus invites the heavy laden to come to Him — not after they feel fixed, but while they are weary. One practical next step: tell one safe person today, “I’m depressed and I don’t want to be alone with it.” If this has been going on for a while, or feels unmanageable, it would also be wise to reach out to a counselor, doctor, pastor, or trusted support person. You don’t have to solve your whole life tonight. Just stay safe, breathe, and take the next faithful step.
